record.title: Langfang consults on four linked AI-economy vouchers in a policy draft
record.summary: On 2026-09-04, Langfang's Development and Reform Commission opened consultation on a draft that proposed four linked AI-economy vouchers: annual caps of RMB 10 million for compute, RMB 4 million for tokens, RMB 2 million for data and RMB 4 million for models. The proposal also describes eligibility and subsidy rules across the four categories. This is a draft consultation notice, not an adopted policy; the reviewed material does not establish implementation, spending or outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Langfang's Development and Reform Commission published a consultation notice for a draft titled Four Measures to Guide Innovation and Development of Langfang's Computing-Power Industry on 2026-09-04, with public comments invited through 2026-10-03.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The draft proposes annual caps of RMB 10 million for compute vouchers, RMB 4 million for token vouchers, RMB 2 million for data vouchers and RMB 4 million for model vouchers, with stated subsidy and award rules across those categories.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected notice does not establish that the draft was adopted, remains in force, received budget appropriations, issued awards or produced delivered compute/data/token services or economic outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The adopted disposition, final instrument and effective date after the consultation period are not established.
No appropriation, award, redemption or settlement data establish whether proposed voucher caps were funded or used.
The draft contains no evaluation of delivered service, additionality or economic results.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and funded, the proposal would establish a local support design spanning compute, token use, data supply and model registration/application, with explicit annual funding caps and eligibility terms. That could change local firm access to AI inputs, but this is a consultation draft; adoption, spending and results are not established.
limitations: The official notice endpoint returned HTTP 403 in this review; its indexed official-site result exposed the notice and draft clauses, but the linked draft attachment was not independently fetched.
The four caps and eligibility rules are proposed terms in a consultation draft, not confirmed appropriations, awards or disbursements.
No adopted final instrument, implementation rule, recipient list or budget-execution record was located in this bounded check; non-discovery does not establish rejection or non-adoption.
No delivered compute, token service, data asset, model deployment, additionality, firm productivity or public return is measured by the proposal.
brief.summary: On 2026-09-04, Langfang's Development and Reform Commission opened consultation on a draft that proposed four linked AI-economy vouchers: annual caps of RMB 10 million for compute, RMB 4 million for tokens, RMB 2 million for data and RMB 4 million for models. The proposal also describes eligibility and subsidy rules across the four categories. This is a draft consultation notice, not an adopted policy; the reviewed material does not establish implementation, spending or outcomes.

technical.claimed_result: The draft proposes annual ceilings and eligibility rules for compute, token, data and model support; these are proposed policy parameters, not measured technical outcomes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official consultation notice and indexed draft expose the proposal and comment period. No adoption, appropriation or delivery was verified.
technical.mechanism: Proposed compute vouchers reimburse part of eligible compute-resource expenses; token vouchers support token-platform development or token-based applications; data vouchers support dataset/quality-data and data-service activities; model vouchers support algorithm registration and model/application development.
technical.regime: One city-level consultation draft published 2026-09-04, open for comments through 2026-10-03. Proposed annual caps: RMB 10 million compute, RMB 4 million token, RMB 2 million data and RMB 4 million model vouchers.
technical.strongest_baseline: A prior Langfang compute-voucher program is documented separately in the archive, but no matched evidence compares its delivered services or outcomes with this proposed four-category revision.

brief.title: Langfang consults on four linked AI-economy vouchers in a policy draft
brief.why_it_matters: Local AI support often focuses on subsidizing compute access. Langfang's consultation draft would extend the proposed support architecture to token use, data preparation/purchases and model registration or application. The design is worth comparing with other municipal programs, but the proposal's legal status and practical effects remain unknown.
